title: People's confidence can change when they set reminders
body: In a 2015 experiment, participants could move objects on a screen to remind themselves of later actions. The less confident they were about remembering, the more they used reminders, even after the researchers accounted for memory ability.
takeaway: When a missed task would matter, set a reminder based on the consequence as well as how sure you feel.
visual: a person placing a small object beside a front door as a reminder

title: Relating an item to yourself can help you remember it
body: A 1997 review found that people remembered items better after judging how the items related to themselves. In many of the experiments, people thought about whether a word described them or simply processed its meaning.
takeaway: For a new idea, think of a situation in your own life that would illustrate it.
visual: a person reviewing a small stack of photographs at a writing desk
